tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

formats.description: Content formats to extract (default: ['markdown'])

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content, filtering out navigation, footers, etc.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in extraction

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to exclude from extraction

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content to load

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

type.description: Type of action to perform

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element

milliseconds.description: Time to wait in milliseconds (for wait action)

key.description: Key to press (for press action)

actions.description: List of actions to perform before scraping

schema.description: Schema for structured data extraction

removeBase64Images.description: Remove base64 encoded images from output

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

search.description: Optional search term to filter URLs

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery and only use HTML links

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

includeSubdomains.description: Include URLs from subdomains in results

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

excludePaths.description: URL paths to exclude from crawling

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl

allowBackwardLinks.description: Allow crawling links that point to parent directories

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

oneOf.description: Webhook URL to notify when crawl is complete

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Ignore query parameters when comparing URLs

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status

id.description: Crawl job ID to check

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,
    "lang": "en",
    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of search results (with optional scraped content).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

filter.description: Search filter

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.description:
Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

tools.name: firecrawl_deep_research
tools.description:
Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

formats.description: Content formats to extract (default: ['markdown'])

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content, filtering out navigation, footers, etc.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in extraction

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to exclude from extraction

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content to load

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

type.description: Type of action to perform

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element

milliseconds.description: Time to wait in milliseconds (for wait action)

key.description: Key to press (for press action)

actions.description: List of actions to perform before scraping

schema.description: Schema for structured data extraction

removeBase64Images.description: Remove base64 encoded images from output

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

search.description: Optional search term to filter URLs

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery and only use HTML links

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

includeSubdomains.description: Include URLs from subdomains in results

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

excludePaths.description: URL paths to exclude from crawling

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl

allowBackwardLinks.description: Allow crawling links that point to parent directories

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

oneOf.description: Webhook URL to notify when crawl is complete

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Ignore query parameters when comparing URLs

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status

id.description: Crawl job ID to check

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,
    "lang": "en",
    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of search results (with optional scraped content).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

filter.description: Search filter

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.description:
Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

tools.name: firecrawl_deep_research
tools.description:
Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

tools.name: firecrawl_deep_research
tools.description:
Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

formats.description: Content formats to extract (default: ['markdown'])

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content, filtering out navigation, footers, etc.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in extraction

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to exclude from extraction

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content to load

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

type.description: Type of action to perform

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element

milliseconds.description: Time to wait in milliseconds (for wait action)

key.description: Key to press (for press action)

actions.description: List of actions to perform before scraping

schema.description: Schema for structured data extraction

removeBase64Images.description: Remove base64 encoded images from output

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

search.description: Optional search term to filter URLs

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery and only use HTML links

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

includeSubdomains.description: Include URLs from subdomains in results

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

excludePaths.description: URL paths to exclude from crawling

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl

allowBackwardLinks.description: Allow crawling links that point to parent directories

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

oneOf.description: Webhook URL to notify when crawl is complete

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Ignore query parameters when comparing URLs

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status

id.description: Crawl job ID to check

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,
    "lang": "en",
    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of search results (with optional scraped content).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

filter.description: Search filter

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

formats.description: Content formats to extract (default: ['markdown'])

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content, filtering out navigation, footers, etc.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in extraction

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to exclude from extraction

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content to load

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

type.description: Type of action to perform

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element

milliseconds.description: Time to wait in milliseconds (for wait action)

key.description: Key to press (for press action)

actions.description: List of actions to perform before scraping

schema.description: Schema for structured data extraction

removeBase64Images.description: Remove base64 encoded images from output

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

search.description: Optional search term to filter URLs

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery and only use HTML links

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

includeSubdomains.description: Include URLs from subdomains in results

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

excludePaths.description: URL paths to exclude from crawling

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl

allowBackwardLinks.description: Allow crawling links that point to parent directories

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

oneOf.description: Webhook URL to notify when crawl is complete

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Ignore query parameters when comparing URLs

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status

id.description: Crawl job ID to check

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,
    "lang": "en",
    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of search results (with optional scraped content).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

filter.description: Search filter

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.description:
Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

tools.name: firecrawl_deep_research
tools.description:
Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).

{

    "url": "https://example.com",

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",

    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,

    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.description:
Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

tools.name: firecrawl_deep_research
tools.description:
Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

tools.name: firecrawl_search

Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**

  "name": "firecrawl_search",

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

formats.description: Content formats to extract (default: ['markdown'])

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content, filtering out navigation, footers, etc.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in extraction

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to exclude from extraction

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content to load

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

type.description: Type of action to perform

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element

milliseconds.description: Time to wait in milliseconds (for wait action)

key.description: Key to press (for press action)

actions.description: List of actions to perform before scraping

schema.description: Schema for structured data extraction

removeBase64Images.description: Remove base64 encoded images from output

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

search.description: Optional search term to filter URLs

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery and only use HTML links

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

includeSubdomains.description: Include URLs from subdomains in results

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

excludePaths.description: URL paths to exclude from crawling

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl

allowBackwardLinks.description: Allow crawling links that point to parent directories

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

oneOf.description: Webhook URL to notify when crawl is complete

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Ignore query parameters when comparing URLs

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status

id.description: Crawl job ID to check

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,
    "lang": "en",
    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of search results (with optional scraped content).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

filter.description: Search filter

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.description:
Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

tools.name: firecrawl_deep_research
tools.description:
Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

Conduct deep web research on a query using intelligent crawling, search, and LLM analysis.

**Best for:** Complex research questions requiring multiple sources, in-depth analysis.
**Not recommended for:** Simple questions that can be answered with a single search; when you need very specific information from a known page (use scrape); when you need results quickly (deep research can take time).
**Arguments:**
- query (string, required): The research question or topic to explore.
- maxDepth (number, optional): Maximum recursive depth for crawling/search (default: 3).
- timeLimit (number, optional): Time limit in seconds for the research session (default: 120).
- maxUrls (number, optional): Maximum number of URLs to analyze (default: 50).
**Prompt Example:** "Research the environmental impact of electric vehicles versus gasoline vehicles."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_deep_research",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "What are the environmental impacts of electric vehicles compared to gasoline vehicles?",
    "maxDepth": 3,
    "timeLimit": 120,
    "maxUrls": 50
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Final analysis generated by an LLM based on research. (data.finalAnalysis); may also include structured activities and sources used in the research process.

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to analyze (1-1000)

tools.name: firecrawl_generate_llmstxt
tools.description:
Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response

tools.name: firecrawl_scrape
tools.description:
Scrape content from a single URL with advanced options.

**Best for:** Single page content extraction, when you know exactly which page contains the information.
**Not recommended for:** Multiple pages (use batch_scrape), unknown page (use search), structured data (use extract).
**Common mistakes:** Using scrape for a list of URLs (use batch_scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get the content of the page at https://example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_scrape",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "formats": ["markdown"]
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Markdown, HTML, or other formats as specified.

formats.description: Content formats to extract (default: ['markdown'])

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content, filtering out navigation, footers, etc.

includeTags.description: HTML tags to specifically include in extraction

excludeTags.description: HTML tags to exclude from extraction

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content to load

timeout.description: Maximum time in milliseconds to wait for the page to load

type.description: Type of action to perform

selector.description: CSS selector for the target element

milliseconds.description: Time to wait in milliseconds (for wait action)

key.description: Key to press (for press action)

actions.description: List of actions to perform before scraping

schema.description: Schema for structured data extraction

removeBase64Images.description: Remove base64 encoded images from output

tools.name: firecrawl_map
tools.description:
Map a website to discover all indexed URLs on the site.

**Best for:** Discovering URLs on a website before deciding what to scrape; finding specific sections of a website.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which specific URL you need (use scrape or batch_scrape); when you need the content of the pages (use scrape after mapping).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl to discover URLs instead of map.
**Prompt Example:** "List all URLs on example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_map",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com"
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of URLs found on the site.

search.description: Optional search term to filter URLs

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery and only use HTML links

sitemapOnly.description: Only use sitemap.xml for discovery, ignore HTML links

includeSubdomains.description: Include URLs from subdomains in results

limit.description: Maximum number of URLs to return

tools.name: firecrawl_crawl
tools.description:
Starts an asynchronous crawl job on a website and extracts content from all pages.

**Best for:** Extracting content from multiple related pages, when you need comprehensive coverage.
**Not recommended for:** Extracting content from a single page (use scrape); when token limits are a concern (use map + batch_scrape); when you need fast results (crawling can be slow).
**Warning:** Crawl responses can be very large and may exceed token limits. Limit the crawl depth and number of pages, or use map + batch_scrape for better control.
**Common mistakes:** Setting limit or maxDepth too high (causes token overflow); using crawl for a single page (use scrape instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Get all blog posts from the first two levels of example.com/blog."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_crawl",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com/blog/*",
    "maxDepth": 2,
    "limit": 100,
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "deduplicateSimilarURLs": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Operation ID for status checking; use firecrawl_check_crawl_status to check progress.

excludePaths.description: URL paths to exclude from crawling

ignoreSitemap.description: Skip sitemap.xml discovery

limit.description: Maximum number of pages to crawl

allowBackwardLinks.description: Allow crawling links that point to parent directories

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow crawling links to external domains

oneOf.description: Webhook URL to notify when crawl is complete

ignoreQueryParameters.description: Ignore query parameters when comparing URLs

tools.name: firecrawl_check_crawl_status

id.description: Crawl job ID to check

tools.name: firecrawl_search
tools.description:
Search the web and optionally extract content from search results.

**Best for:** Finding specific information across multiple websites, when you don't know which website has the information; when you need the most relevant content for a query.
**Not recommended for:** When you already know which website to scrape (use scrape); when you need comprehensive coverage of a single website (use map or crawl).
**Common mistakes:** Using crawl or map for open-ended questions (use search instead).
**Prompt Example:** "Find the latest research papers on AI published in 2023."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_search",
  "arguments": {
    "query": "latest AI research papers 2023",
    "limit": 5,
    "lang": "en",
    "country": "us",
    "scrapeOptions": {
      "formats": ["markdown"],
      "onlyMainContent": true
    }
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Array of search results (with optional scraped content).

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (default: 5)

lang.description: Language code for search results (default: en)

country.description: Country code for search results (default: us)

filter.description: Search filter

formats.description: Content formats to extract from search results

onlyMainContent.description: Extract only the main content from results

waitFor.description: Time in milliseconds to wait for dynamic content

tools.name: firecrawl_extract
tools.description:
Extract structured information from web pages using LLM capabilities. Supports both cloud AI and self-hosted LLM extraction.

**Best for:** Extracting specific structured data like prices, names, details.
**Not recommended for:** When you need the full content of a page (use scrape); when you're not looking for specific structured data.
**Arguments:**
- urls: Array of URLs to extract information from
- prompt: Custom prompt for the LLM extraction
- systemPrompt: System prompt to guide the LLM
- schema: JSON schema for structured data extraction
- allowExternalLinks: Allow extraction from external links
- enableWebSearch: Enable web search for additional context
- includeSubdomains: Include subdomains in extraction
**Prompt Example:** "Extract the product name, price, and description from these product pages."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_extract",
  "arguments": {
    "urls": ["https://example.com/page1", "https://example.com/page2"],
    "prompt": "Extract product information including name, price, and description",
    "systemPrompt": "You are a helpful assistant that extracts product information",
    "schema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "name": { "type": "string" },
        "price": { "type": "number" },
        "description": { "type": "string" }
      },
      "required": ["name", "price"]
    },
    "allowExternalLinks": false,
    "enableWebSearch": false,
    "includeSubdomains": false
  }
}
```
**Returns:** Extracted structured data as defined by your schema.

urls.description: List of URLs to extract information from

schema.description: JSON schema for structured data extraction

allowExternalLinks.description: Allow extraction from external links

enableWebSearch.description: Enable web search for additional context

includeSubdomains.description: Include subdomains in extraction

Generate a standardized llms.txt (and optionally llms-full.txt) file for a given domain. This file defines how large language models should interact with the site.

**Best for:** Creating machine-readable permission guidelines for AI models.
**Not recommended for:** General content extraction or research.
**Arguments:**
- url (string, required): The base URL of the website to analyze.
- maxUrls (number, optional): Max number of URLs to include (default: 10).
- showFullText (boolean, optional): Whether to include llms-full.txt contents in the response.
**Prompt Example:** "Generate an LLMs.txt file for example.com."
**Usage Example:**
```json
{
  "name": "firecrawl_generate_llmstxt",
  "arguments": {
    "url": "https://example.com",
    "maxUrls": 20,
    "showFullText": true
  }
}
```
**Returns:** LLMs.txt file contents (and optionally llms-full.txt).

url.description: The URL to generate LLMs.txt from

maxUrls.description: Maximum number of URLs to process (1-100, default: 10)

showFullText.description: Whether to show the full LLMs-full.txt in the response
